## c52-w5 (release #52, wave W5: swing 4h; class numbers assigned at merge)

- **Class c52-w5-a: a "this level is invalid" marker erased by the very action it permits.** The swing's through-close marker (`swingTouch.Through`) was cleared (`FirstTouch = nil`) the moment the ISB entry fired, so a later wick-touch-and-close-back in the same 4h candle armed an ordinary reject (and superseded/cancelled the resting ISB order) at a level the mentor declared invalid ("chỉ đi kiếm Insaba" [D5.2 p2 @20:41-21:04]). Probe: for every state flag that gates a path off, grep each writer; does any branch clear it as a side effect of the path it still allows? Rule: the invalid marker stays latched until the 4h flip; the fire sets a separate `ISBFired` so the ISB itself is once per invalid level, which in practice means ONCE PER 4h CANDLE: while Through stays latched a new through-close is never recorded, so ISBFired is never re-cleared before the 4h flip. That latch is a trade-set reduction (10-21 replay: two later long 2-contract SWING4H ISB arms, 15:05 and 15:45 CT, dropped because the 14:30 ISB had fired) and is an OPEN OWNER CALL, not a settled rule: the course states no once-only limit. Pins `TestSwing4hW5ISBFireKeepsThroughLatched`, `TestSwing4hW5ISBDoesNotRearm`.
- **Class c52-w5-b: a pattern read without the field that gives it a direction.** The swing ISB took its side from the approach and never looked at candle 1's colour, and the close-back bar could be its own inside bar (one beat early). The course: candle 1 closes back, then ONE more 5m beat for an inside bar of it, and candle 1's colour sets the side (red short, green long) [D1.4 p1 @09:20-09:36, D5.2 p1 @21:25-21:40]. Probe: every call to `IsISB` must be next to an `ISBDirection` read of the same `prev`, and the "close back" test must be applied to `prev`, not only to the inside bar. Rule: swing ISB = prev closed back across the line AND `ISBDirection(prev)` == the swing side AND b inside prev. Pins `TestSwing4hW5ISBNotOnTheCloseBackBar`, `TestSwing4hW5ISBWrongColourCandle1Refused`, `TestSwing4hW5ISBCandle1MustCloseBack`.
- **Reference:** c52-w5 `fix/c52-w5`; `kernel/mentor/swing4h.go` Through branch. Three older fixtures (eval_test warm-swing pair, swing_risk_test) relied on the old wrong-colour pair and were re-cut with a real red close-back candle 1.

## c52-w2 (release #52, exit drive: resonance + candle trail; class numbers assigned at merge) — a "no cap" that only logs, a window counted on the wrong clock, and an exit rule that skipped a leg

- **Class c52-w2-a: a stored decision the wire never carried.** The mode-A runner was meant to run ("cho nó chạy" [D2.4 p1 @02:24-02:47]; m186 chose "OFF = no cap"), but OFF only LOGGED "NOT sent" and nothing removed the runner's PHL/PLH take-profit, so every resonance runner still exited at its old cap, shy of the old high; the code comments ("native TP REMOVED") described a send that never happened, the NT8 AddOn cannot drop a TP leg (`HandleModifyBracket` reads `new_take_profit <= 0` as "leave untouched"), and the knob default read ON for `rc == nil`, OFF for a loaded strategy and ON on five more surfaces (guide, panel, registry, effective settings, struct comment). **Probe:** for every "removed / cancelled / uncapped" comment, find the frame that does it and the AddOn handler that honours it; for every knob default, grep ALL surfaces and the nil path. **Rule:** OFF means the TP is parked 600 points out through the real `modify_bracket` (bounded retries on later candles; one-bracket positions untouched), one default everywhere.
- **Class c52-w2-b: a window counted on a different clock than the thing it measures.** The resonance window ("within 3 candles after the fill, count 1, 2, 3") counted closed 1m bars with the fill candle as bar 1, while after 09:00 CT every ISB is read on the 2m (a mother plus an inside bar needs two closed 2m candles), so most 2m resonance ISBs arrived at 1m bar 4-8 and were refused. **Probe:** for every N-candle window, name the frame of the candle in the source sentence and the frame of the counter; test the boundary on the 2m and 5m, not only the 1m. **Rule:** `mentorLivePos.candlesAfterFill` counts candles of the entry frame after the fill candle (the fill candle itself is NOT counted: ours, mentor question B18); window 1..3.
- **Class c52-w2-c: a rule applied to the leg that is easy to reach, not the leg the course names.** (B1) The candle-trail path moved only the RUNNER legs, so leg 1 (most of the contracts) sat at break-even until its TP filled while the course keeps the live risk:reward at 1:1 ("lúc nào cũng phải maintain ở mức 1-1", D1.2 p1 @15:56-16:07); (B2) the resonance break-even fired at +0.25R on EVERY leg including leg 1, although the course justifies the BE by the 1:1 partial already sold. **Probe:** for every per-leg rule list which legs the code touches per mode and diff against the source sentence's legs. **Rule:** leg 1 gets `2c - T` while unfilled (after the arming candle, never wider, never on/through the market, only with `mentor_be_before_partial` ON); a split resonance position's BE waits for the confirmed partial and moves the runner legs only.
- **Reference:** c52-w2 `fix/c52-w2`; pins `TestC52W2A3KnobDefaultsAgree`, `TestC52W2A3UncapIsSentByDefault`, `TestC52W2A3UncapRetriesAfterAFailedSendThenStops`, `TestC52W2A3UncapTargetsOnlyTheFinalRunner`, `TestC52W2B18ResonanceWindowCountsEntryFrameCandles`, `TestC52W2B2ResonanceBEWaitsForThePartialAndMovesTheRunnerOnly`, `TestM151ResonanceMovesLeg1`, `TestC52W2B1Leg1KeepsTheLive11StopInCandleMode`, `TestC52W2B1KnobOffMovesNothingBeforeThePartial`.

## c52-w3 (release #52, level-arm lifecycle; class number assigned at merge) — a cancel that does not spend the thing it cancelled, read on a frame the order was not placed on
- **Symptom:** a resting level order cancelled by a later candle closing through the level was re-placed at the SAME price on the very next tick (reproduced on the TestLevelOrderRestsAndCancels tape: cancel at tick N, same buy stop 29393 at N+1), because the through-candle still "touches" the support from above, the touch stays TouchReject with the same RefBar, and nothing recorded that the reference had been used. Separately the close-through read the last 1m bar even for a 2m/5m order, so a 1m wick-close inside a still-forming 2m candle cancelled an order whose 2m candle would close back.
- **Probe:** for every code path that CANCELS an order the evaluator itself placed, ask what state stops the very next tick from re-placing it (the DropArm RefusedLevelTouch mechanism is the model), and for every candle test ask which frame the order was read on and whether the test reads that frame's last CLOSED candle.
- **Rule:** the close-through cancel spends the touch reference (`RefusedLevelTouch[key] = Touches[key].RefBar.CloseTime`; the 15:00 expiry does NOT spend it) and `LevelArm.ExecTFMin` stores the placement frame; the close-through is tested on the last closed bucket of that frame. A NEW reference candle may trade again. Moving-line and rolling-PHL arms are untouched.
- **Reference:** c52-w3 `fix/c52-w3`; `kernel/mentor/eval.go` `levelArmCancels`, `LevelArm.ExecTFMin`; pins `TestC52W3CancelSpendsReference`, `TestC52W3CancelRecordsReferenceBar`, `TestC52W3ExpiryCancelDoesNotSpend`, `TestC52W3ArmCarriesItsFrame`, `TestC52W3CloseThroughReadOnTheArmsFrame`. B13 (broken key level backtest) and B23 (box re-flip) are NOT built: the course contradicts itself (D1.3 Uno flip vs D5.2 "invalid") and the plan marks both as one owner/mentor Uno ruling.

## c52-w10 (release #52, 5m pullback warning; class number assigned at merge) — a warning that knows the trend but not the entry side
- **Symptom:** the X11 "5m pullback" size cut (`pullbackWarning5m`) fired when the previous 5m candle was green and this one broke its low, and was stamped on EVERY ISB regardless of side. The course warns about trading WITH the 5m trend into the pullback ("market chuẩn bị pullback ... hạn chế vô lệnh") and mirrors it for a downtrend. A SHORT ISB taken in the uptrend's own pullback was cut, the opposite of the lesson, and the downtrend mirror did not exist. "5m uptrend" was only "the previous candle is green".
- **Probe:** for every flag stamped on an intent, ask which SIDE the source sentence applies to and whether the stamping site receives the side; for every "trend" boolean, check whether it reads structure or one candle colour; check that a mirror exists for every one-directional rule. A test that sets the flag by hand never sees a missing side parameter: drive the Tick.
- **Rule:** the evaluator computes the warned SIDE (long in a 5m structure uptrend whose last closed candle broke the prior low; short in a downtrend whose last candle broke the prior high; none without a clear structure) and `isbFlagsFor(cur, side, ...)` stamps the flag only on that side. Scope (ISB and reverse ISB only) and the mandatory cut are unchanged and disclosed; extending to PHL/PLH and making it optional are open owner calls.
- **Reference:** c52-w10 `fix/c52-w10`; `kernel/mentor/eval.go` `pullbackWarning5m` / `isbFlagsFor`; pins `TestPullbackWarning5mDirectionAware`, `TestPullbackWarnOnISBTick` (normal ISB emit site, ~2322) and `TestPullbackWarnOnReverseISBTick` (reverse ISB emit site, ~2480, driven through `Tick` on `isbReverseFixture` with a synthetic 5m history: warned side carries the flag, unwarned side does not). Mutants RED: drop the side compare; drop the mirror; flip the side argument at the normal site; flip the side argument at the reverse site (the review found this one survived until the reverse pin was added). Caveat: the positive "warned side carries the flag" case at the NORMAL site is checked by calling `isbFlagsFor` on the Tick-set state, because a candle that broke the prior 5m low also flips the 5m trigger to sell and the warned long is refused upstream; the reverse pin pins the trigger LONG by hand.

## c52-w11 (release #52, invented-constant knobs; class numbers assigned at merge) — a number we made up that no card, registry row or test admits to
- **Class c52-w11-a: an invented constant stated as the method.** Ten numbers decided real trades and were written as if the course supplied them, with no knob and (for two) a guide line that implied a source: the evening "slow" cutoff of 100 pts and its 15:00-cumulative window (`eveningSlow`; owner Q6 fixed no number), the near-box distance of 2 x risk and its extension to PHL/PLH (course shows an ISB only; the guide said "recommended: 2 - D3.2 p1 @21:53"), the ISB size-cut "old high/low" band of +/-2 and "in range" gap of 50 (borrowed from the ping-pong gate), the 5-pt PHL target shy, the 2m ISB stacking cancel on candle 4 (the course counts 1m candles only) and the missing tiny-stop exception. **Probe:** for every numeric literal in `kernel/mentor/eval.go`, `isb.go`, `box.go` and `phl.go` that gates, sizes or times an entry, find the course sentence that states the number; a literal with no sentence needs a `Config` field, a `risk_control.mentor_tuning` knob (default = the old literal), a knob-registry Note that says "OURS, not the course" and a guide card that says the same. A guide line that cites a lesson for a number the lesson does not give is the same defect.
- **Class c52-w11-b: a second copy of a config the evaluator already carries.** The box-return walk in `Tick` built `DefaultBoxCfg()` while `latchBoxes` read `e.Cfg.Box` (nothing sets `Cfg.Box` today, so no live divergence, but the first caller to configure a box frame would have split the draw from the walk). **Probe:** grep for `Default*Cfg()` calls inside a method of a type that holds the same config; use the held field (`baseBoxCfg()`).
- **Rule:** every knob in this wave defaults to the value the kernel hard-coded before, so an unset key changes nothing; `ISBInRangeGapPts` 0 inherits `PingPongMinGapPts` so a stored ping-pong gap keeps reading the same; pointer knobs (`near_box_room_multiple`, `phl_target_shy_pts`, `isb_old_extreme_pts`) let an explicit 0 through (near-box OFF, target AT the extreme, exact touch). ## c52-w12 (release #52, docs / guide / comment sweep; class number assigned at merge) — prose that describes a rule the code or the course no longer says
- **Symptom:** after waves W1-W11 the guide, the knob registry and code comments still described superseded behaviour: a "Never between two trigger lines" card (there is ONE trigger line; the zone is FTGL to the buy line), a "Line partials (deferred ... release #31)" card that contradicted the shipped runner partial, a quoted mentor sentence ("buổi tối mà nó đi chậm thì đánh khung 5 phút thôi") that is not in the transcript (X11 @18:03 says "Trade khung 5 phút only"), the keypair-ratio note naming "the largest recent 1m candle" while the code reads the current closed candle, a "NOT built in #25" line for the fresh RTH pair that m429 built, a header calling `LocationVerdict` the production gate for the ISB (it is test-only and the ISB is not location-gated), and comments claiming a reverse ISB runs the ISB stacking arithmetic (it never writes `State.ISBArms`) or that a trendline entry has an unknown frame. Four course gaps (doji candle 1, two losses = place off for the day, the swing 30-pt re-arm, sub-minute frames) and seven parked items (B12 more line partials, B14 EMA switch-off, B15 5m wick zone, B16 nine-line test, B17 30s inside bar, B24 VWAP, B26 2m size cut) were not disclosed anywhere.
- **Probe:** after any behaviour wave, grep guide/registry/comments for the old rule's key words (`deferred`, `NOT built in #`, `largest recent`, `two trigger lines`, `default 30`, `ExecTFMin == 0`), and for every quoted foreign-language sentence open the .srt at the cited timestamp and compare word for word; for every "ours" constant ask whether the card says so.
- **Rule:** prose that states a rule is part of the change that moved the rule (GUIDE CONTENT LAW); a quotation mark means a transcript line; an invented fail-closed choice (doji refusal, two-loss day-off, swing re-arm distance, sub-minute substitution) is labelled "OURS" with the course line it does not cover; a parked course item gets a "Not built" note naming the open question instead of silence. `LocationVerdict` stays (test-only), never deleted.
- **Reference:** c52-w12 `fix/c52-w12`; doc-only, no trade change (REAL_DAY_REPLAY: not applicable, no replay-visible code touched); pins `mentor guide — c52 W12 doc sweep` in `web/src/guide/content/mentor.test.ts` (stale phrases absent, every parked item disclosed, the three "ours" labels present; mutant = reinstating the old card titles goes RED).

## m434 (release #51; class number assigned at merge) — a per-Tick recomputation: a new rule that re-derives history on EVERY Tick

- **Symptom:** #51's m428 R5 (non-adjacent pairing) scored every earlier same-role swing against every later one, each with an O(bars) crossed-between-anchors scan, rebuilt from scratch on every 1-minute Tick (the live bot runs the same Tick). `TestR22PHLTargetExtremeHasTheTradeRole` went 6.5s -> 40s and `go test -cover ./kernel/mentor` hit the CI 1-hour timeout (run 40294325268). Also: the HTF build re-bucketed the whole window into 2m once per swing pair, and the 5m/1h/4h buckets were rebuilt in several places per Tick.
- **Probe:** for every new rule inside Tick, ask "what is its cost per Tick as the trading day grows?" Look for nested loops over swings x bars, an aggregation (`barsTF` / `closedBucketsTF`) inside a loop, and a pure helper that re-buckets what the evaluator's per-Tick memo already holds. Run `go test -run <replay test> -cpuprofile` on a full-session replay for every wave that touches Tick, and compare `BenchmarkM434Tick*` before and after. CI runs the package under `-cover`, which multiplies the cost of hot loops: a wave is not done until the `-cover` run is timed too.
- **Rule:** a rule that scans history is computed once per Tick (or incrementally per swing), shares the per-Tick bucket memo, tests the cheap discriminator (standing, not a crossed scan) first, and keeps its output byte-identical: an optimisation lands with a golden per-tick digest of the intents stream, State JSON, notes and ChartLevels/ChartTrendlines recorded from the unoptimised code (`testdata/m434_tick_identity.golden`).
- **Finding left unchanged (no behaviour change allowed):** `flatNearAtTime` (HTF pairs) is documented as "candles that closed at or before tMs" but `closedBucketsTF(bars, 2, tMs)` only drops the still-forming tail, so it reads the LAST 20 traded-frame candles of the whole window, not those before the anchor. Also `carryIntradayLines` appends carried lines in Go map order (display order of ChartTrendlines is not deterministic; the identity digest compares the set).
- **Reference:** m434 `fix/m434-mentor-tick-perf`; `partnerPicker`, `trendlineCrossed`, `flatNearFromB2`, `trendlinesBuildTFFrames`; pins `TestM434TickOutputIsByteIdentical`, `TestM434BestPartnerMatchesReference`, `TestM434PartnerPickSkipsLosingCrossedScans`, `TestM434CrossedMatchesWickBeyond`; benchmarks `BenchmarkM434Tick`, `BenchmarkM434TickR22`.

## m431 (release #52; class number assigned at merge) — a cleanup placed mid-function that a later stage can outrun
- **Symptom:** on the real 2026-10-23 tape an ISB arm registered at 12:22 CT (`isb-13` live, `isb-17` in the fixture), was never emitted, stayed in `State.ISBArms` for two ticks, and a `cancel_arm` for a never-authored order went out at 12:24. The deferred flag-wall target pass (`applyFlagWallTarget`, refusal `flag_wall_room`) dropped the entry AFTER the m425a S1 un-register pass, and the arm snapshot was taken at one mid-Tick point. Separately, the real-day replay harness (`refusalFor`) named only a fixed list of refusals at the single nearest bar, so a kernel refusal the kernel DID make (trade 690: `isbrev_target_below_floor`; 683: `phl_no_old_extreme_on_side`; 667: `level_invalid_first_touch`; 671: `near_box`) read "no named refusal".
- **Probe:** for every "undo what registration did" pass, list the stages that can still drop the object AFTER the pass runs (defers, late filters, target rewrites) and every return path that skips it; run the real day and assert at every tick that registered state is a subset of what left the function. For every attribution harness, ask whether it names ANY refusal the system can make (not a hand-kept list) within the frame the live author instant can differ by, and whether it can still fail.
- **Rule:** ONE exit pass in `Tick` (`unregisterDroppedArms`, after the leave-stamp and the deferred flag-wall pass, on every return path) un-registers every arm registered during the Tick whose entry did not leave; arms held before the Tick are untouched. The harness attributes any kernel refusal counter plus refusal-shaped trader counters within +-5 min (one 5m frame) of the live arm and stays able to fail.
- **Reference:** m431 `fix/m431-phantom-arm-flagwall`; `kernel/mentor/eval.go` `heldArmIDs` / `unregisterDroppedArms`; pins `TestM431NoArmWithoutAnEmittedEntryOnTheRealTape`, `TestM431DroppedEntryUnregistersEveryArmKind`, `TestM431RefusalAttribution*`; fixtures `testdata/m431_state_20261023_0830.json.gz` + `testdata/m431_window1500_1m_20261023_0829.csv.gz` (production State at the 08:30 tick + the 1500-bar window, dumped from the real-day replay).

## m432 (release #52; class number assigned at merge) — an outage that announced itself only to places nobody was looking
- **Symptom:** 2026-10-25 17:00 CT to 2026-10-26 03:40 CT the bot was blind ~10.5 h (NT8 running and linked, its Tradovate data connection off); "FEED DOWN" went only to the in-app alert center and the log, and the owner learned of it from the CTO. After the reconnect a 640-minute hole could not refill because NT8 had no history for the span; the cure is an owner action in NT8 (Reload All Historical Data) and nothing told him.
- **Probe:** for every P0/P1 alert kind, list the surfaces that carry it. Is there ANY that reaches the owner when he is not looking at the app? For every "needs a manual step by the owner" log line (UNFILLED, STUCK, HELD), is there an alert with the exact step in words? For every episode-shaped alert, is there a matching "over" message, and does it fire once per episode and not once per trader or per minute?
- **Rule:** ops P0s that matter while the bot cannot trade (feed-down while CME is open, trader down, dead-man stuck, protection) also go out through `internal/ownerpush` (outbound only, async + bounded queue, one message per episode key, 3 per kind and 30 total per hour (m442 #27: the "8/hour" was a stale figure), scrubbed, never on a friend instance, no-op unbound); recovery gets one message; a hole NT8 cannot refill raises ONE P1 with the instruction, and only while NT8 is linked AND feeding live bars (otherwise it is FEED DOWN's story, and a scale-disagreement hole does not tell him to reload).
- **Reference:** m432 `fix/m432-owner-reachability`; `trader/owner_push.go`, `internal/ownerpush`, `ntTrader.UnfilledHolesFeeding`; pins `TestFeedDownPushesOwnerOncePerEpisodeAndTellsHimWhenItIsBack`, `TestFeedDownPushIsOncePerEpisodeAcrossTraders`, `TestNoOwnerPushWhileCMEIsClosed`, `TestOwnerPushKindsAreExactlyTheOpsP0Set`, `TestOwnerPushNeverFiresOnAFriendInstance`, `TestUnfilledHoleRaisesOneP1AndOneOwnerMessage`, `TestUnfilledHoleIsReportedOnlyWhileNT8IsFeedingLiveBars`, `internal/ownerpush` suite. Test trap: the CME-open leg reads `ownerPushClock`, never the wall clock (a bare `time.Now()` made the first draft of the feed-down pin pass only while CME was open).

## m433 (release #52; class number assigned at merge) — a gate leg that can only be answered by a source that is down, with no path to "known flat"
- **Symptom:** NT8 linked over TCP, broker connection down (a closed-market Sunday). The installation gate's per-trader legs 2 (api_positions: "NT8 account positions unknown") and 4 (working_orders: order snapshot older than 2N) failed by F4/F12 design, and nothing the owner could do changed them — the update was blocked until the broker returned. Leg 2 only failed on a process with no positions frame at all (a restart in the broker-down state), leg 4 only on a process that HAD frames (the book goes stale after 60s); no test drove either state through `InstallationGateStatus` with the production cutover seam (the fixture stubs it with passing legs).
- **Probe:** for every gate leg answered by the broker, drive the state "link up, broker silent" through the production gate and ask what the leg says in (a) a fresh process and (b) a process that already saw frames. Is there any evidence the leg could quote that is not the silent source (the LAST answer it gave, persisted)? Does the fixture stub the seam that would show it?
- **Rule:** the installation gate (never `CutoverGateStatus`) accepts a failing leg 2/4 only when the failure is "no fresh broker answer" AND the CME session is closed AND the DB and armed ledger are flat AND the broker's last order snapshot and last positions frame (in memory and/or persisted) were flat with no source saying otherwise; a known position, a working order, a live book, an open market, disagreeing sources, or no last answer at all refuses (unknown is not flat). The rule's pass quotes its evidence.
- **Reference:** m433 `fix/m433-install-gate-broker-down`; `trader/installation_gate_m433.go` (`m433Relax`), `store/nt_positions_last.go`, `TCPServer.SetPositionsSink`; pins `TestInstallationGateM433*` (no evidence stays closed, persisted flat passes, market open / open position / working order / DB open / placed ledger row / one-sided evidence / live book / disagreeing sources refuse, stale in-memory flat passes, CutoverGateStatus stays strict), `TestTCPServer_PositionsSinkReceivesNonFlatCount`, `TestNTPositionsLastUpsertGet`.

## m436 (release #53; class number assigned at merge) — a second path to the same entry that skips the gates the first path carries
- **Symptom:** c52 W6 flipped the rolling PHL/PLH (`kernel/mentor/rolling_phl.go`) to default ON. It built its entry through `PHLPLHGatedR2Levels` only, so it never ran the LOCATION bans that sit inline in the level touch loop (`eval.go`): `phl_5m_box_ban` / `phl_15m_box_ban` / `phl_30m_box_ban`, `phl_mid_range`, `phl_mid_range_boxed`, `near_box`, `keypair_candle_too_big`. With a standing 5m ISB box {105..125} and a close at 113 the roll armed (armed=1, refusals empty) where the level path refuses `phl_5m_box_ban` (the live funnel counts thousands of those a day). Two siblings in the same file: `levelTouchRejectActive` walked ALL of `State.Touches`, including entries of levels that had left the level set, so one orphan `TouchReject` switched a whole side off silently for the rest of the day and across days; and the roll took its side from the gate-aware `HTFVerdict`, which returns an EMPTY side whenever the 4h/1h gate is off (everywhere outside 08:30-09:30 CT and the print window), so the roll cancelled every resting stop at 09:30 and started none after.
- **Probe:** for every new entry path (rolling, swing, box, reverse-ISB, planner) list the refusals the older path carries inline and ask which of them the new path calls. A refusal written inline in a loop body is a gate no second caller can reach: grep the loop body for `e.refuse(` names, then grep the new path for each name. For every "does any X own this" scan over a map, ask whether the map is pruned when the key's source disappears. For every value read from a gate-aware helper, ask what it returns when the gate is off, and test the new path at a wall-clock time OUTSIDE the fixture's window.
- **Rule:** location bans live in ONE helper both paths call (`phlLocationBan`, `phlNearBoxRefuses`), never copied; the rolling path names its refusals `rolling_<level-path name>` and counts once per reference candle; a ban also cancels a resting roll. A "does a level own the entry" scan reads only levels still in the set. The rolling trend side is the gate-aware verdict inside the gate's windows and the 4h direction alone outside them.
- **Reference:** m436 `fix/m436-rolling-phl-location-bans`; pins `TestM436RollingRefusedInsideStandingISBBox`, `TestM436RollingBoxBanCancelsRestingRoll`, `TestM436RollingRefusedMidRange`, `TestM436RollingRefusedBetweenBoxes`, `TestM436RollingRefusedNearBox`, `TestM436RollingRefusedKeypairCandleTooBig`, `TestM436LevelPathStillCountsBoxBan`, `TestM436OrphanTouchDoesNotBlockRolling`, `TestM436RollingTradesOutsideTheHTFGateWindow`; `testdata/m434_tick_identity.golden` re-recorded (deliberate change).

## m437 (release #53; class number assigned at merge) — an expiry judged on the wall clock before the data it covers is consumed; a fill-relative window restarted by a rebuild
- **Symptom (1):** the swing resting order expires at bucket end - 1ms, and the tick that finalises the bucket's LAST 5m bar runs at exactly the bucket end. `SwingTick` dropped `Pending` on `now >= ExpiryMs` at the top of the tick, before the bar walk reached that last bar, yet NT8 keeps the order live until the expiry, so a trade-through on that bar was a REAL fill that the kernel never tracked: `Swing.Pos` stayed nil, no BE at +1R, no hold-close, and SWING4H is exempt from EOD/news flat, so only its stop or target ended it (about 1 resting order in 48). Existing swing tests used `now = open + 60s` and never reached a bucket-end tick.
- **Symptom (2):** a restart-rebuilt PHL/PLH position restarts `BarsSinceFill` / `FramesAfterFill` at 0, so the 3-candle resonance window re-opened on the 2nd-4th candle after the boot; a same-side ISB flipped a mature runner to mode A and (#52 A3, knob OFF) uncapped its take-profit. Rebuilt ISB positions were already latched (`ISBPartialDone`); resonance had no equivalent.
- **Probe:** for every expiry or timeout in a state machine that walks closed bars, ask which bar is the LAST one the thing can still act on, and whether the drop happens before or after that bar's check; drive the production clock convention (`now = CloseTime+1`) through the boundary tick, not `open + 60s`. For every counter that gates a fill-relative window, ask what a rebuild/restart sets it to and whether the window can re-open.
- **Rule:** an order is expired against the BARS: a bar that opens after the expiry never fills it, every bar up to and including the last bar of the bucket gets its fill check, and the drop happens after the walk (`expireSwingPending`). A rebuilt position never re-runs a fill-relative window (`ResonanceSpent`, beside `ISBPartialDone`).
- **Reference:** m437 `fix/m437-swing-expiry-fill-order`; `kernel/mentor/swing4h.go` `SwingTick` / `expireSwingPending`, `trader/mentor_live_pos.go` `ResonanceSpent`; pins `TestSwingExpiryFillOnLastBarOfBucketIsTracked`, `TestSwingExpiryUnfilledOrderExpiresCleanly`, `TestSwingExpiryBarAfterExpiryNeverFills`, `TestM437RebuiltPHLPositionNeverReopensResonanceWindow`, `TestM437LiveFilledPHLPositionStillArmsResonance`. Trader side checked: the NT8 order is cancelled Go-side at the ledger `ExpiryMs` (`armExpired`, `sweepDueExpiriesAtReopen`), the same instant the kernel now stops expecting a fill, so a fill before the expiry is real on both sides.

## m438 (release #53; class number assigned at merge) — an alert channel whose own failure modes silence the alerts it exists for
- **Symptom:** the #52 owner push (m432) had five ways to fail the owner exactly when it mattered. (1) `unprotected_position` on the PLACE verdict minted `now.UnixMilli()` into its event id every 1-minute pass, so a refused/unconfirmed stop wrote a new P0 row and a new push each minute; eight went out in eight minutes and the shared 8/hour budget then dropped FEED DOWN and trader-down too. A dropped P0 was never retried (the alert row is written once and only a NEWLY written row pushes). (2) The Telegram sender used `tgbotapi.NewBotAPI` (an `http.Client` with no timeout) and logged the raw `*url.Error`, whose text is the request URL, bot token included. (3) The 65-74 character trader ids were redacted by the scrubber as token-shaped, so the phone message could not say which trader. (4) The unfilled-hole message promised "the bot picks it up on its next re-request" but the slow re-requests are capped at 8 (about 2 h); a later reload was never re-asked and the message omitted the restart the log line itself names. (5) `ReplayDisagreed` was the process-lifetime disagreeing-replay count copied onto every hole. The first fix baselined it per hole but still on the cache-wide counter, so an unrelated SYMBOL's disagreement while the hole was open still steered the message (review round 2: a baseline on a shared counter is per-hole only for the past, not for the future).
- **Probe:** for every notification channel ask: what happens on the Nth repeat (does the dedupe key carry a clock?), can ONE kind use the whole budget, is a dropped message ever re-offered, what bounds a single send in time, what does the error text contain (a URL with a credential in it), does the text survive its own scrubber with the one identifier the reader needs, and is every number in the text a count for THIS subject or a global.
- **Rule:** an event id is an EPISODE id (stamped on the transition in, cleared on the transition out), never a per-pass clock; the budget is per KIND with a backstop above kinds x budget; a refused message is held (bounded, aged) and re-offered by the beat, and withdrawn when it stops being news; every send has an HTTP timeout AND a worker-side deadline; errors from a client that puts credentials in URLs are redacted before they reach the log; the text names the subject by display name; an instruction in a message must be true for as long as it is the reader's latest word (state the horizon and the follow-up step, and send the follow-up when the horizon passes); a per-subject figure is a delta from a baseline taken when the subject was created, on a counter that is itself keyed by the subject (symbol), not a shared one; every wiring line that makes a held message safe (Cancel on recovery, sweep of per-episode state when the position goes) has its OWN pin through the production caller, because a unit pin on the primitive does not notice the call being deleted.
- **Reference:** m438 `fix/m438-owner-push-hardening`; `internal/ownerpush` (`kindOf`, `Retry`, `Cancel`, `deliver`), `telegram/update_result.go` (`redactTelegramErr`, `ownerSendTimeout`), `trader/protection_reconciler.go` (`protectionPlaceEpisode`), `trader/owner_push.go` (`ownerPushTraderLabel`, `unfilledHoleSpentBody`), `trader/ninjatrader/bar_holes.go` (`disagreedAtDetect`, `UnfilledHole.SlowSpent`), `provider/ninjatrader/bar_overlap_verdict.go` (`OverlapDisagreedFor`); pins `TestHeldFeedDownIsWithdrawnWhenTheFeedComesBack`, `TestPlaceEpisodeIsSweptWhenThePositionCloses`, `TestUnfilledHoleReplayDisagreedIgnoresAnotherSymbol`, `TestOverlapDisagreedIsCountedPerSymbol`, `TestProtectionPlaceEpisodeRaisesOneAlertAndOnePush`, `TestOneKindCannotStarveAnother`, `TestDroppedOwnerPushIsRetriedByTheMonitorBeat`, `TestNotifyOwnerNeverLogsTheBotToken`, `TestNotifyOwnerCannotHangOnABlackHole`, `TestStuckSenderCannotHangTheWorker`, `TestOwnerPushNamesTheTraderNotTheRedactedID`, `TestUnfilledHoleOwnerMessageStaysTrueAfterTheCap`, `TestUnfilledHoleReplayDisagreedIsPerHole`.
- **Known limit (not fixed):** a held P0 other than FEED DOWN (e.g. `NO stop`) is re-offered for up to 90 minutes (`holdTTL`) and can arrive after the stop was placed; only FEED DOWN is withdrawn on recovery. The 'about 2 hours' re-ask horizon counts CME-open time only (the re-ask gate defers while CME is closed), so wall-clock time can be longer.
- **Decision recorded (item 4):** the re-request cap (8, #23 review P2-3) is deliberate and unchanged. The message was made true instead of the cap removed: it states the ~2 h horizon and the restart a late reload needs, and a second P1 + push goes out when the cap is spent.

## m440 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — state keyed by (symbol, side) judging a DIFFERENT position of the same side
- **Symptom:** `MoveStopToBreakeven` judged the B1 widen ban against `t.stopLoss["MNQ:LONG"]`, a value keyed by side with no memory of which position wrote it. The armed (limit / stop) entry placers never wrote that key and nothing cleared it on close, so row 706's break-even (29700, SENT 00:42:36 UTC 10-29, log_events 341258; closed whole at sl 01:00:38, 341281) stayed in the key and pos 712 (next long, entry 29522) had every break-even at 29522 refused as a "widen from 29700" from 03:38:27 UTC for ~85 min (341830-342140). 95 `stop-widen REFUSED` rows since 10-23 (76 x 29522<29700, 19 x 29032<29181 on pos 696), every one a retry of a legitimate tighten. The position ran on its wide original stop while the log said BE was being tried. Found by reading the live log, not the diff: the refusal line reads like a working safety net.
- **Probe:** for every map keyed by (symbol, side) or any shared key, list the writers and ask who clears it when the thing it describes ends, and whether every entry path (market, limit, stop-entry, materialized/restart) re-seeds it. For every safety ban that compares a new value to a remembered one, ask WHOSE value is remembered, and grep the live log for the ban's refusal line: a ban that fires every minute for an hour is a stale reference, not a ban.
- **Rule:** a guard compares a move against the stop of the signal being moved (per-signal record, else the side-keyed value only when it is bound to that signal or is an unbound `SetStopLoss`); an armed entry that reached the wire re-seeds the side key bound to its own signal; a WHOLE `position_close` (leg 0) for the owning signal clears it (a split-leg close never does: a runner is alive; a close naming another signal never does). The genuine widen on the same position stays refused.
- **Other readers of `t.stopLoss` checked:** `placeEntry` (legacy path reads it only after `SetStopLoss` for that entry; the clear-on-close tightens the "must be called before" guard rather than weakening it); trail (`auto_trader_trailing`), mentor BE (`mentor_actions`), mentor trail (`mentor_mode`) and planner auto-BE all reach it only through `moveStopWire` -> `MoveStopToBreakeven` (fixed here); the protection reconciler reads `KnownStopForSignal` (per-signal, not side-keyed, unaffected); the CSV `Trader` has its own copy of the same pattern (`trader.go:104,176`), deprecated path, not changed.
- **Not fixed (reported):** `resolveEntrySignalID` returns the LAST entry's signal id (`lastEntrySignalID`), including a not-yet-filled armed order, and `entryOrderID[side]` is never cleared on close, so a side-keyed move can address a pending or dead signal rather than the live position's.
- **Reference:** m440 `fix/m440-be-stale-side-stop`; `trader/ninjatrader/tcp_trader.go` (`stopLossOwner`, `liveStopForMoveLocked`, `reseedSideStopOnEntry`, `ForgetSideStopOnClose`), `close_sync.go`; pins `TestN1_SecondLongBEBelowFirstLongsStopIsSent`, `TestN1_SecondShortBEAboveFirstShortsStopIsSent`, `TestN1_RealWidenOnTheSamePositionStillRefused`, `TestN1_MaterializedPositionIsNotJudgedByAnEarlierSignalsStop`, `TestN1_PositionCloseFrameClearsTheOwnersSideStopOnly`, `TestN1_LegacyBracketEntryStopStillBansAWiden`, `TestN1RealDayReplay`. Mutants: full revert RED (6 pins); BE reads the bare side key RED (materialized pin); no re-seed RED (widen pin); no clear-on-close RED (close pin).

## m441 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — a state machine that clears its state when it EMITS an action, not when the action is CONFIRMED; a guard that runs before the branch it was never meant to pre-empt
- **Symptom (1, system check N2):** the swing's `Swing.Pos` was cleared only when the hold-close was emitted, never on the stop or target fill. A swing stopped out at 22:58 (pos 707) stayed "open" in the evaluator, and hours later it could emit a BE (moving ANOTHER trade's stop, signal-keyed by side) or a market close — which the AddOn runs as a Flatten of the whole instrument, whatever the side. The executors checked only that the arm's LEDGER ROW had filled (it stays `filled` forever), never that the account still held the position.
- **Symptom (2, N3):** `MovedBE = true` and `Pos = nil` were set at EMIT. A refused or failed BE (no live bracket, unreadable book) and a refused hold-close were final: the swing sat on its full stop, or was carried past the 4h rule, and the refusal line said "retried next 4h read" while nothing retried. The BE also used the side-keyed `moveStopWire` (compared against a stale per-side stop, class N1) with none of the F1 broker-book verification the intraday legs have.
- **Symptom (3, #15):** the hold-close was a market `CloseLong/CloseShort`, i.e. `Account.Flatten`, which also cancels every resting arm on the account. X8 already exits with a marketable limit for exactly that reason.
- **Symptom (4, P2-3, trade 707):** the one-setup-per-approach "not yet re-armed" guard ran BEFORE the through-close branch, so a touching 5m bar that closed THROUGH the 4h line while the guard was set was skipped without latching `Through`. The next bar read the other side of the line as a fresh approach and armed a normal reject at a level the course makes invalid for the whole 4h candle (10-28 17:35 CT close 29633 < line 29645.53 -> 17:40 short arm 475 -> position 707, -200).
- **Probe:** for every "emit an intent, then clear/latch state" pair ask who CONFIRMS the intent and what the state does if the answer is no (is the emit the same event as the effect?). For every action the evaluator issues against a shared resource (an account, an instrument), ask what proves the actor still owns that resource at the moment of the act, and what the wire call really scopes to (read the AddOn handler, not the Go helper name). For every guard placed ahead of a branch, ask whether it was written to stop ARMING and is therefore swallowing an INVALIDATION. Replay the real bars of the loss (10-28 17:10-17:50 CT), not a synthetic tape.
- **Rule:** the evaluator keeps a swing's BE and hold-close owed until the executor reports back (`Evaluator.SwingBEApplied`, `Evaluator.SwingEnded`); the BE is re-emitted once per closed 5m bar, the hold-close likewise. Both executors act only when the account holds a position carrying the arm's OWN signal id (an OPEN `trader_positions` row or a working `<signal>-sl` in a fresh broker book) and report `ended` when the position is provably over; `mentorSwingReconcile` runs at the top of every tick and clears a stopped-out swing before it can emit. The BE rides `mentorMoveLegStop` (signal-scoped, never-widen against the broker, F1 verdict). The hold-close is `mentorMarketableExitLimit` (shared with X8) with one market close if the position is still open past the grace. A close through the line is latched before the re-arm guard.
- **Reference:** m441 `fix/m441-swing-exit-state`; `kernel/mentor/swing4h.go` (`manageSwingPosition`, `BEApplied`, `Ended`, the guard/through order), `kernel/mentor/eval.go` (`SwingBEApplied`, `SwingEnded`), `trader/mentor_swing_exit_state.go`, `trader/mentor_actions.go` (`mentorMoveStopBE`, `mentorClosePosition`), `trader/mentor_exit_drive.go` (`mentorMarketableExitLimit`); pins `TestSwingBERetriesUntilApplied`, `TestSwingHoldCloseRetriesUntilEnded`, `TestSwingEndedByStopNeverActsLater`, `TestSwingThroughCloseNotSwallowedReal1028`, `TestSwingThroughCloseNotSwallowedByGuardShort`, `TestMentorSwingStoppedOutNeverCloseOrMovesLater`, `TestMentorSwingReconcileClearsStoppedOutSwing`, `TestMentorEvalOnceReconcilesStoppedOutSwing`, `TestMentorSwingBERefusedThenAppliedReportsReceipt`, `TestMentorSwingHoldCloseUsesMarketableLimitThenFallback`, `TestMentorSwingRefusalTextNamesTheRealRetry`, `TestMentorSwingWorkingBracketIsProofOfLife`, `TestSwingMaxStopPtsIsNotASkipInSwingRejectIntent`. `TestM434TickOutputIsByteIdentical` now emulates a perfect executor (receipts after every BE / close) so the golden recorded at 75707f1ed stays byte-identical.
- **Known limits (not fixed here):** (a) the AddOn's `close_position` is a whole-position close on the account (the limit is sized to what the account holds; `quantity` is ignored), so a swing hold-close still takes any OTHER same-side position with it — only a C# change can scope it; (b) the 100-pt clean-reject stop is still armed (`MaxStopPts` is not used as a skip in kernel `swingRejectIntent`; its default is the SIZING ceiling the trader reads in `mentorSwingCeiling`, which caps a swing at 2 MNQ when the stop reaches it — `mentorSwingWideStopCap`) pending mentor Q43; (c) a close through the line that does not reach the 5-pt placement offset (`touchesLineApproach`) is still not a "touch" and latches nothing. (d) the market-close fallback is not latched in the sent record (unlike X8's `X8MarketFallback`): while the positions row still reads OPEN, each later closed 5m bar can re-send a market close (a whole-instrument Flatten on the AddOn), bounded by the ownership proof — "one" market close holds only per bar. (e) the swing BE now routes through `mentorMoveLegStop` like the intraday legs: after an earned but unapplied BE, if price has pulled back through the entry, it takes the stop-through-the-market path and `mentorCloseLegAtMarketWire`, a whole-instrument Flatten (rare: needs several refused retries first). (f) log noise: `close_sent` and its log repeat per call while the limit is in flight, and the ownership WARN for an unreadable table / row repeats on every 1m tick via `mentorSwingReconcile`.

## m442 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — an alert that is not TRUE, or that reaches nobody
- **Symptom:** (1) `ownerpush` marked the episode key seen and spent the hourly budget AT ENQUEUE, and the Telegram sender returned nothing: a getMe/sendMessage failure or timeout was indistinguishable from a delivery, so a lost FEED DOWN / unprotected-position push was never re-offered (N4). (2) Held pushes and the dedupe map were memory only; a restart (the deploy IS a `kill -9`) dropped every held P0 (#24). (3) The boot line and the checklist said "8/hour"; the code is 3 per kind and 30 total (#27). (4) Nothing told the owner the bot died or restarted (#28). (5) A rejected exit (`position_close_rejected`) was one log line and a counter (#19). (6) The core complaint: refusals sat in the logs for days (95 refused break-evens 10-23..10-29) because each one is ONE line and nobody reads a line. (7) The stalled-setup P1 counted the trader's own trading-window / day-stop refusals as a stall; 15 of the 27 "Mentor setup stalled" rows in `log_events` (11 `window:`, 4 `done_after_win:`) were exactly that (#9).
- **Probe:** for every notification channel: does the sender return its OUTCOME, and does a failure leave the message eligible (key un-seen, budget refunded, held with backoff)? what survives a `kill -9` (held, seen, in-flight)? is every number the boot line prints READ from the constant? who tells the owner the process started, and how the last one ended? For every refusal site: is the Nth repeat louder than the first? For every "stalled/never happened" alarm: which of the counted refusals are the operator's own rules, and does the alarm still fire for the real causes (stale_data / stale_intent / sources)?
- **Rule:** the sender returns an error (`nil` delivered · `ErrNotBound` skipped, never retried · anything else failed → un-see + refund + hold with 30 s..15 min backoff, aged out at `holdTTL`); success is logged and counted; the counters ride `/api/health` `owner_push` (absent when no pusher runs); held + in-flight + seen persist atomically to `data/data.db.ownerpush.json` (0600, no deletion, temp file overwritten by the next write); the boot push names rev + how the last process ended (clean-signal / not-clean / first-boot); refusal sites call `ownerpush.NoteRefusal` (3 in 10 min per class+trader+subject = ONE push per episode, own budget per class); exits NT8 refused raise an ops P0 per episode (`position_close_rejected`, event id = episode, never the frame time); a stall alarm excludes the operator's own rules (`Policy` counter, recorded at the refusal site) and says how many.
- **Reference:** m442 `fix/m442-owner-alerts-truth`; `internal/ownerpush` (`onFailed`, `state.go`, `storm.go`, `Limits`, `BootMessage`), `telegram/update_result.go` (`SendOwnerText`), `trader/close_rejected_alert.go`, `trader/refusal_storm.go`, `trader/ninjatrader/close_sync.go` (`OnCloseRejected`), `telemetry/setup_stall.go` (`Policy`), `trader/mentor_stall_alarm.go` (`mentorStallPolicyRefusal`); pins `TestFailedSendIsHeldUnseenAndRetriedWithBackoff`, `TestOwnerPushRetriesAFailedTelegramSendEndToEnd`, `TestHeldAndSeenSurviveARestart`, `TestLimitsTextIsReadFromTheConstants`, `TestBootMessageNamesRevAndHowTheLastProcessEnded`, `TestM442RejectedExitRaisesOneP0AndOneStormPushOverTheRealWire`, `TestStormFiresOncePerEpisodeAtTheThreshold`, `TestM442StopWidenRefusedThreeTimesPushesOneStorm`, `TestM442SwingBERefusedThreeTimesPushesOneStorm`, `TestM442StopMoveNotAppliedReachesTheOwnerOverTheVerifyLoop`, `TestM442WindowRefusalsAreNotAStall`, `TestM442StallPolicyClassificationAgainstRealLogRows`.
- **Known limit (not fixed):** a send abandoned at its 30 s deadline that then completes late is delivered AND retried (a duplicate P0 is the cheaper error than a lost one). The boot push cannot say WHY a `kill -9` happened, only that the last exit was not a clean signal exit. `never_add`, `no_chase` and `same_side_working` refusals still count toward the stall alarm (they were not in the ruling; say if they are the operator's own rules too).

## m443 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — a panic-path UI that paints success from "the request returned", and a poller that cannot say "I cannot reach you"
- **Symptom (N6):** `EmergencyFlatButton` rendered whatever JSON came back in GREEN. The server answers HTTP 200 `{triggered:false, reason}` when NT8 is down or the broker is not a ninjatrader bridge (`api/handler_risk.go`), and 401 on an expired token; the component never read `r.ok` or `triggered`. In a panic the owner could believe a position was flattened that never left.
- **Symptom (#39):** `StatusBanner` ignored the SWR error, so a dead backend rendered nothing, and a failed poll after a good one kept the last good CME/FEED line on screen. A page frozen on old numbers looked alive.
- **Probe:** for every control that sends a command, list the response shapes the handler can return (200 with a refusal flag, 4xx/5xx, non-JSON proxy page, network error) and ask which of them the component colours green. For every poller that renders a status line, ask what is on screen after the poll fails — absent, stale, or an explicit "unreachable".
- **Rule:** green requires 2xx AND the handler's positive flag (`triggered === true`); everything else is red `NOT SENT: <reason>`. A status poller shows an explicit unreachable state on a failed poll (null counts as failed), that state wins over stale data, and it clears on the next success.
- **Reference:** m443 `fix/m443-panic-ui-truth`; `web/src/components/trader/EmergencyFlatButton.tsx` (`interpretForceFlat`), `web/src/components/common/StatusBanner.tsx`; pins `EmergencyFlatButton.test.tsx` (8 response shapes), `StatusBanner.test.tsx` (`BOT UNREACHABLE` x5).

## m444 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — a detector that only runs on the event it exists to catch the absence of
- **Symptom:** MNQ 1m was missing 2026-10-26 17:00–21:56 CT (297 open minutes) while MNQ 3m/5m and ES 1m were whole, for days, and no surface knew. The hole detector (`observeLive`) ran only when a live 1m bar arrived; its boot scan reached back only to the CURRENT session open; a hole beyond NT8's replay window was DROPPED from the tracker and `/api/health` the moment it was retired (so even a detector that re-ran would have re-announced it forever); the hole counters were per boot and read 0 after the restart. The 10-26 outage itself (restart 12:07 CT, NT8 TCP link DOWN until 08:36 next day) was flagged loudly (3477 FEED DOWN lines) — what was not flagged was the HISTORY that stayed missing afterwards (UNFILLED was a log line only, no push, no dashboard).
- **Probe:** for every detector of "something did not happen", ask what drives it. If the driver is the arrival of the thing that is missing (a bar, a heartbeat, a fill), the absence is invisible exactly when it matters. List its evidence window against the oldest gap it must still know about, and ask what the list shows after the item is retired, after a restart, and after the event source goes quiet. For every cross-feed pair (1m vs 3m/5m, bars vs ticks) ask whether one feed's presence is evidence that the other's absence is a fault.
- **Rule:** an absence detector reads the STORE on a clock (boot + every 10 min, rolling 7 CME session days, one indexed single-column read per symbol), through the one calendar and the one tracker; it never waits for a live arrival. A gap with no stored bar on one side is judged by cross-frame evidence (a stored 3m/5m bar covering an open minute proves it traded). A retired hole stays LISTED (state `retired`) so a re-scan cannot re-announce it; an episode is announced once. Counters that matter to the operator are re-derived from the store (`bars_hole_audit.unfilled_holes_7d`), not accumulated per boot. The operator-facing sentence is ONE constant (`BarsMissingAction`) shared by the dashboard banner and the owner push.
- **Reference:** m444 `fix/m444-bar-gap-audit`; `trader/ninjatrader/bar_gap_audit.go` (`auditPass`, `auditSpans`, `applyAuditLocked`), `bar_holes.go` (`holeStateRetired`), `store.OpenTimesBetweenOn`, `TCPServer.SubscribedRoots`, `api/handler_health.go` `bars_hole_audit`, `trader/owner_push.go` `unfilledHoleBody`, web `StatusBanner` `missing-bars-banner`; pins `TestAuditSpansFindTheReal1026MNQHole` (real 10-26 rows, `testdata/mnq_20261026_1m_gap.json`), `TestAuditSpansCrossFrameCatchesAHoleWithNoLaterOneMinuteBar`, `TestAuditFindsAnOldHoleWithNoLiveArrival`, `TestAuditAnnouncesAnOldHoleOnceAndKeepsItListed`, `TestAuditClosesAHoleTheStoreNowHolds`, `TestAuditFoundRetiredHoleReachesTheOwnerRead`.
- **Known limit (not fixed):** a hole further back than 4800 1m bars (about 3.5 CME sessions) cannot be re-read at all and is RETIRED (listed, never asked; clears when it leaves the 7-session audit window). A trailing gap with no 3m/5m evidence (the feed delivering nothing) is FEED DOWN's, not this audit's. Root cause of the missing MNQ 1m span INSIDE NT8 is inferred [B], not proven: the 21:57 start of the stored 1m rows is exactly the bars_back=2000 edge (2000 CME-open minutes) of the 10-28 08:17 replay [A, arithmetic], NT8 served MNQ 1m from 21:57 on later and ES 1m for 17:00-21:56 on 10-27, so 17:00-21:56 may well exist in NT8 beyond the 2000-bar window every subscribe uses. The first cut said "NT8 never served it" - not proven.
- **Review rounds (m444, round 1-2) — three more ways the same detector lies:**
  - *A cross-frame rule needs the frames to cover the same history.* The bot subscribes with `bars_back=2000` on EVERY timeframe, so 1m reaches ~33 h back, 3m ~4 days, 5m ~7 days. "3m/5m evidence before the first stored 1m bar" is therefore the NORMAL shape of any fresh install or new contract, not a hole; the first cut raised MISSING BARS and a P1 owner push on it (4980 min on a fixture, 2329 min on real ES 12-26 data). Only the TRAILING edge (and "no 1m at all") is judged; a hole with 1m on both sides is `findBarHoles`'. Pins `TestAuditFreshContractWithHigherFramesFurtherBackOpensNoHole`, `TestAuditGraceKeepsTheNewestMinutesOutOfTheWindow`.
  - *A set that is added to and never pruned outlives the thing it describes.* `barHoleTracker.checked` keeps the old contract's key after a roll, so the audit re-found and re-retired the old contract's holes every 10 minutes (WARN pair + counters) until restart. The audit reads only the contract `CurrentContract` names. Pin `TestAuditDoesNotRescanAContractTheSubscriptionRolledAwayFrom`.
  - *An instruction must be true for the state it is attached to.* (Round 2 narrowed which state: see below - the "retired" text now applies only to a hole beyond the deepest ask; a hole the deep ask reaches is asked for, not written off.) A RETIRED hole is by definition past the replay window (a bot restart re-reads only the last 2000 1m bars), so "Reload All Historical Data, then restart the bot" can never fill it; the banner and the phone push now say "the bot cannot refill it" and when it clears, and the reload line is kept for UNFILLED holes only (the banner leads with the biggest unfilled hole). Pins `TestRetiredHoleBodyDoesNotTellTheOwnerToReloadOrRestart`, web `StatusBanner.test.tsx` "a retired hole says the bot cannot refill it".
  - **Known limit (not fixed):** there is no owner-visible acknowledge/clear for a retired hole; it leaves the list only when it ages out of the audit window (7 CME sessions by default) or the store gains the bars.
- **Review round 2 (m444) - three defects of "a state transition with no consumer", and one false absolute:**
  - *"The bot cannot refill it" was false.* The first cut retired every hole past the subscription's bars_back=2000 and told the owner so on the phone, the banner and the guide. A deep path already existed (`RequestDeepBarsBackfill`, the arbiter's) and the 10-26 hole sat ~2800 open minutes back. Now the tracker asks NT8 for such a hole with a DEEP 1m request (`TCPServer.RequestDeepGapBackfillAt`: 1m only, on the same admission/budget as every gap re-request, 2 scheduled asks + 2 slow, sized to the hole at every send). Only a hole beyond the deepest ask is retired. Pins `TestHoleBeyondTheStandardReplayIsAskedForDeeplyAndFills` (fills end to end through the persister), `TestDeepHoleHasASmallerBudgetAndUnfilledNamesTheRightLever`, `TestDeepHoleThatSlidesBeyondTheDeepestAskIsRetired`, `TestPlainWireWithoutADeepPathRetiresABeyondReplayHole`, `TestDeepGapBackfillIsOneTimeframeClampedAndOnTheSameAdmission`, `TestDeepHoleOwnerMessagesDoNotPromiseARestartFixesIt`.
  - *A reach constant must be the MINIMUM of every stage it flows through.* The arbiter's 8640 bars pass the replay-hold, which keeps the NEWEST 5000 rows per key: an 8640-bar replay would silently lose its OLDEST 3640 rows - the very rows a deep hole sits in - the measure would see the hole still open and the owner would be told "NT8 has no history" for rows the bot threw away. The deep ask is capped at 4800 and a compile-time guard in `replay_hold.go` ties it to the hold. **Latent, not fixed (outside this wave): the bar-arbiter `action=backfill` default of 8640 has the same loss.** Found by the first end-to-end deep test, whose replay also showed a replay is released to the store only when it overlaps live minutes (the ring must be able to judge its scale).
  - *When a state is added (retired), every place that used to remove on it must be re-read.* With `BARS_GAP_AUDIT_DAYS=0` nothing closes or ages out a retired hole, so it sat on the banner and `/api/health` until a restart and took a tracker slot (review 1, defect 2): with the audit off it is dropped as before. Retired holes also no longer count toward the 32 working slots (a separate 128-entry list). Pins `TestRetiredHoleIsDroppedWhenTheAuditIsOff`, `TestRetiredHolesDoNotEatTheWorkingSlots`.
  - *A branch that is the only exit for a state needs its own pin.* `applyAuditLocked`'s aged-out case is the only way a retired hole leaves; a mutant `case false && ...` stayed green. Pin `TestRetiredHoleAgesOutOfTheAuditWindow` (through `auditPass`). Likewise the `isOpen` guard on the cross-frame evidence: `TestAuditEvidenceInTheDailyBreakIsNotEvidence`.
  - **Known limits (noted, not fixed):** a hole first live-detected starting at 16:00 (the break) and re-found by the audit after a restart starts at 17:00, so its event id (which includes FromMs) can push once more; with the NT8 link down since boot `CurrentContract` is unknown and the audit audits nothing until the ACK (FEED DOWN covers that span); a partial 1m stall reads as a transient audit hole with one extra re-request.

## m448 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — a backup nobody has restored, and a data failure that is only discoverable by forensics
- **Symptom:** the DB is backed up twice a day (C1 timer), and nothing had ever opened the newest backup since the 2026-08-13 manual check: a corrupt or empty backup would have been found on the day it was needed. Separately, a day's data truth (bars expected vs stored, holes that never filled, a final frame dropped by the ingest queue, a clock step) existed only as since-boot counters and log lines; the per-minute ingest summary even SWAPS its counters to zero, so "how many final frames were lost today" had no answer at all. The owner learned of data trouble from the CTO, days later.
- **Probe:** for every durable artifact the system depends on in a disaster (backup, snapshot, export), ask when it was last RESTORED (not written) and by what; whether the check opens the copy read-only, runs the engine's own integrity check, and compares a content sanity (rows, newest stamp) against the artifact's OWN time rather than now; and whether the result is a file the next report can read. For every counter a report would print, ask whether anything ZEROES it (a Swap(0) in a summary) and what the reader sees after that; whether it is since-boot or per-session and whether the line says which; and what the line prints when the source is not wired (must be n/a, never 0).
- **Rule:** `deploy/backup-restore-test.sh` restores the newest backup into its own mktemp dir, requires `PRAGMA integrity_check` = `ok`, traders >= 1, positions >= 1 and a newest 1m bar within 120 h of the backup's own mtime, prints one `RESTORE-TEST OK|FAIL` line, writes a NEW result file (append-only) and exits non-zero on failure; it removes only its own `restore-test.*` dir. A weekly timer unit is provided (owner installs it). The nightly report (`internal/datareport`) reads every figure, prints n/a when a source is unwired or belongs to another session day, labels since-boot counters with the boot time, counts unresolved P&L instead of summing it, and is sent once per session day (O_EXCL marker) through the ownerpush public API. A per-minute-swapped counter that a report needs gets a cumulative twin folded under one lock (`IngestDropTotals`).
- **Reference:** m448 `fix/m448-data-report-backup-check`; `internal/datareport`, `deploy/backup-restore-test.sh`, `deploy/systemd-user/vl-restore-test.{service,timer}`, `provider/ninjatrader/bar_persist.go` (`IngestDropTotals`), `main_datareport.go`; pins `TestCollectCountsExpectedVsStoredAndTheFeedDownRuns`, `TestMixedAndOffScaleRowsAreNotStoredBars`, `TestDefaultExpectedMirrorsTheHoleTrackerOnGoodFriday`, `TestTradesAndPnLByTraderAndSetupUseTheCorrectedColumnOnly`, `TestRefusalsRepeatedMoreThanThreeTopFiveNoClockSkew`, `TestRefusalsAreNAWhenTheTableIsForAnotherSessionDay`, `TestNothingWiredPrintsNAEverywhereNeverAZero`, `TestReportReadsEveryFigureAndFitsTheOwnerPushLimit`, `TestTickSendsOncePerSessionDayInsideTheWindowThroughOwnerPush`, `TestRestartDoesNotResendTheSameSessionDay`, `TestFriendInstanceNeverSendsTheReport`, `TestRestoreResultReadsNewestAndFlagsFailureAndOverdue`, `TestIngestDropTotalsSurviveTheMinuteSwap`, `TestDataReportSourcesBindToTheLiveCounters`, `TestRestoreTest*` (deploy).
- **Review round 1 fixes (D1, D2, N1-N5):** a figure with a window and a DISTINCT needs a pin with rows on both sides of each boundary and several traders on one event (`TestFeedDownAlertsAreDistinctEpisodesInsideTheHalfOpenSession`); EVERY since-boot counter on the page is labelled, and an in-memory table that restarts with the process says so when the boot is later than the session start (`TestBadPrintsAndRefusalsCarryTheSinceBootLabel`); "the market had a day" comes from the calendar, never from what the store holds (`TestAnEmptyStoreOnAnOpenCalendarDayStillSendsTheReport`); a scheduler loop under `safe.GoNamed` dies for good on one panic, so the tick is wrapped in `safe.Must` (`TestStartKeepsTickingAfterATickPanics`); a report that is cut from the end must put its most serious line near the top (`TestAFailedRestoreTestIsNeverTheLineThatGetsCut`); bars outside the calendar are counted, not a silent 0/0 (`TestBarsStoredOutsideTheCalendarAreReportedNotAZeroOverZero`).
- **Known limit (not fixed):** the bar-hole, ingest and clock counters are since-boot, so a mid-session restart makes them partial (the line says since boot <time>); a report missed because the bot was down 16:10-17:00 CT is not sent late (the gate table it reads rolls at 17:00; a follow-up could send it marked LATE); a claim-before-send crash loses that day's push (the log keeps the full text); the calendar itself is the kernel's, so a day it wrongly calls closed is only reported as bars stored outside the calendar. The two counters other lanes add (cross-frame mismatches, paused minutes) print n/a until the integrator calls `datareport.Register` for them.

## m445 (release #54; class number assigned at merge) — a safety signal that is produced and displayed but never read by the decision it exists to protect
- **Symptom:** the bar-hole tracker knew every missing stretch of 1m bars (detected, re-requested, measured, declared unfilled) and its only reader was `/api/health`. Every entry path asked a data question — the stale feed, ~75 s — and none asked "are the bars in my window complete?". After the 2026-10-26 reconnect the bot traded on a window with 297 open minutes missing (17:00–21:57 CT, never refilled; the store still has the hole). Two further shapes sat inside the same blind spot: a hole the tracker RETIRED (outside NT8's replay window, or the contract rolled) was simply dropped from its list, so any reader of "open holes" would read it as clear while the minutes were still gone; and an unreadable detector (no store, boot scan not run, a store read failed, detector behind the cache) read as "no holes".
- **Probe:** for every detector/monitor ask who READS it besides the display: grep the consumers, not the producer. For every "open items" list ask what removes an item and whether each removal is a RESOLUTION or a GIVE-UP (give-up must stay visible). For every health/guard read ask what it returns when the source is unknown, not wired, or has not run this process — it must be BLOCKED, never "none found". For a data window ask which frames each consumer reads and how they are built (aggregated from the 1m vs native per frame) and size the window from the code (`mentorBars1mDepth`, `AISVPBarCount`, the 4h EMA 34 span), not a guess.
- **Rule:** ONE fail-closed verdict per symbol (`ntTrader.IntegrityVerdictFor`: a not-filled hole overlapping the path's window, OR the detector unknown) joined with the stale-feed leg, asked at the single admission chain every entry crosses (`admitChain`) and at the mentor's authoring and armed-pass seams; entries only — exits, stops, BE/trail, closes, protection never cross it. A hole the tracker stops chasing is RETAINED and re-measured (`retainRetiredLocked`, `remeasureRetired`); resume is a measurement or the hole aging out of the window, never a timer and never persisted. The pause is announced once (log + owner push + `/api/health trading_paused` + dashboard banner), resting entries are withdrawn with the reason named in the ledger, and an unknown detector is pushed/withdrawn only after a 5-minute grace so a restart is silent.
- **Reference:** m445 `fix/m445-data-integrity-gate`; `trader/ninjatrader/bar_integrity.go` (`IntegrityVerdictFor`, windows), `trader/data_integrity_gate.go` (path table, episode, withdraw), `trader/entry_admission.go` (`dataIntegrityAdmitRefusal`), `trader/mentor_tick.go` / `trader/armed_executor.go` (mentor seams), `trader/withdraw.go`, `api/handler_health.go`; pins `TestIntegrity*` in `trader/ninjatrader/bar_integrity_test.go` (real tracker, real 10-26 data fixture `testdata/mnq_1m_2026-10-26_27_runs.json`, `TestRealCleanDaysNeverPause` on `/tmp/realday-1021|1022|1023`) and `trader/data_integrity_gate_test.go` (one pin per entry path).
- **Round-1 review fixes (same class):** (D1) an API route that puts a MARKET entry on the SIM wire (`POST /api/debug/nt-test-trade`) called the broker adapter directly and so crossed no gate — every route's door to the wire must be an `AutoTrader` seam (`DebugNTTestTrade`), pinned structurally by `TestAPIHasNoDirectBrokerEntryDoor` (no api production file may name a broker entry method) and behaviourally by `TestIntegrityGateRefusesTheDebugTestTradeDoor`; (D2) a detector's COVERAGE is part of its answer — the boot scan stopped at the session open while the gate judged 8160 open minutes, so a restart after the session roll read the older hole as clear (`TestRestartAfterTheSessionRollStillSeesAnOlderHole`); the scan now reaches the deep window and a window older than the coverage is UNKNOWN (`TestAWindowOlderThanTheDetectorsCoverageIsUnknown`); (B) a give-up state must stay MEASURED — a hole whose slow retries were spent was never re-read, so a reload that refilled it never lifted the pause (`TestSpentHoleIsRemeasuredAndResumes`). (W) the SWING4H window was the AI's 34 candles though its 4h EMA is gated on and computed over the 102-candle warm-up (`kernel/mentor.FourHEMA34Warmup`), and every N-candle window was cut THROUGH its oldest candle — windows are now (N+1) candles and the swing one is `IntegritySwingOpenMin` (`TestSwingWindowSeesAHoleTheDeepWindowDoesNot`, `TestIntegrityWindowsEqualTheCodeTheyDescribe` pins it to the mentor constant). Probe: for any "all clear" ask what range it actually looked at versus what the decision reads, and whether every blocking state has an exit that is a measurement.
- **Known limits (not fixed):** the detector judges the stored bars it has read this process — the deep window at boot, then every live bar (the 7-day DB audit is m444's wave and lands holes in the same tracker); a gap of 1–2 open minutes is not a hole (`BARS_HOLE_MIN_GAP_MIN`); the stale-feed leg does not cancel resting entries (unchanged: a 75 s hiccup must not churn the ledger); holes on a contract the subscription rolled away from are retired by the tracker and not counted (the bot reads the current contract's series only).
- **Round-2 review fixes (same class):** (D1) a verdict's WINDOW must cover the state the decision stands on, not only the data it reads each pass: the mentor evaluator's seeded key levels (`kernel/mentor.KeyLevels`, "No lookback cap"), open-HTF lines, day latch and trendlines are walked once over the contract-STITCHED 1m history (`mentorFullKeyLevelHistory`) and live for the process, so the 1500-minute intraday window called a two-session-old RTH hole clear while the levels were built from the holed candles. The doc comments that claimed "every frame is aggregated from this 1500-minute slice" were false for seeded state and are corrected. Two mentor-only legs now close it: the tracker's RTH holes of any age (`ntTrader.IntegrityVerdictForMentor`, asked by `dataIntegrityVerdictAt` for every mentor trader) and the RTH holes in the stitched series the seed walked, measured at every seed and re-seed (`noteSeedSeries` -> `ntTrader.SeriesRTHHoles`, 90-day reach = the 1m retention; resume = a history reload bumps the refill generation, the evaluator re-seeds, the next measurement is clear) (`TestMentorVerdictBlocksAnRTHHoleTwoSessionsBack`, `TestSeriesRTHHolesJudgesTheSeededSeries`, `TestMentorSeededSeriesRTHHoleBlocksUntilTheRefillReseeds` through the real `mentorSeedAtStart` + `mentorReseedOnRefill`, `TestMentorTraderAsksTheKeyLevelVerdictAtEverySeam`, `TestHealthTradingPausedNamesTheMentorSeedLeg`). A first attempt (scan the head contract's whole stored history at boot) was REJECTED on the live store: the stitch cuts the older contract at its last stored bar, so a head-contract hole inside the pre-cut stretch is not in the seeded series while an older-contract hole is, and the head contract's sparse pre-roll import snapshots (one row a day 09-07..09-10, 425 rows 09-11) read as ~1400-minute holes. Probe: for a persisted/seeded state ask how far back its inputs reach, WHICH SERIES they were built from, and judge that series, not a neighbour of it; a doc comment that says "everything is built from X" is a claim to grep, not to trust. (E) a bounded retained list that DROPS its oldest entry turns an old unfilled hole into "clear" once the newer ones fill — the eviction is now remembered and the verdict is UNKNOWN until a restart (`TestRetiredListOverflowIsUnknownNotClear`). (G) a grace measured in wall time counts the weekend: a restart over the closure sat "unknown" for 40 h of CLOSED market and pushed/withdrew 20 s after the Sunday reopen — the unknown clock now starts at the first beat that finds CME open (`TestIntegrityUnknownGraceIsOpenTimeOnly`). (L) a gate that logs a WARN per refusal on a days-long pause floods the log: decision / agent / mentor-authoring refusals now log once per (path, class) episode while every refusal is still counted (`TestIntegrityDecisionRefusalIsLoggedOncePerEpisode`, `TestIntegrityMentorPlacementRefusalIsLoggedOncePerEpisode`).
- **CONTRACT ROLL false pause (round 2, FIXED):** a newly rolled contract is stored sparsely before the bot records it (live store, 12-26: one `historical_import` row a day 09-07..09-10, 425 rows 09-11, dense from 09-14 09:34) and the tracker's boot scan read those stretches as ~1400-minute holes: replaying the real 12-26 rows with a 09-15 08:00 boot blocked ALL THREE windows (intraday on `09-13 17:00–09-14 09:36`; deep and swing on `09-07 … 09-11`) — at every roll the gate would pause mentor intraday for a day, the AI/planner window for ~6 trading days and SWING4H for ~18. `trimPreRecording` drops the LEADING `historical_import` rows of a boot-scan read (the bot was not on the contract yet; the stitch takes those minutes from the older contract); an import row after the first recorded bar is data, and a store with no recorded bar is judged whole (`TestRollInSparseImportsAreNotHoles`). Probe: for every "all clear/not clear" computed from a store, ask what the store holds BEFORE the process started recording and whether that stretch is a loss or simply a time the system was not there.
- **Known limits, round 2:** (1) a hole older than the 90-day reach in the seeded series is not judged. (2) after the Dec roll the stitched series' newest-contract head still follows the stitch cut; a hole in the HEAD contract's pre-cut stretch is not in the series, so the tracker's key-level leg (which does see it, if it is within the boot scan's 24720-minute reach) can pause the mentor on a hole the seed did not walk — fail-closed, and bounded by the reach. (3) the health scope for a tracker-held old RTH hole is `mentor_entries`, and the dashboard banner shows it for every trader (the banner does not know which trader is mentor).
- **Round-4 review fixes, #55 (same class: a check that judges its own reading of the data, not the data):**
  - (D1) A roll seam read as lost data. The stitched series cuts the older contract at its last stored bar and takes the head strictly after it, so a minute only the HEAD stored (2026-09-14 09:36–09:57 CT: MNQ 09-26 hole, MNQ 12-26 `historical` rows) is absent from the series although recorded; round 3 paused every mentor trader for ~45 days on it and told the owner to "reload NT8 history", which replays ~2000 1m bars and cannot reach a days-old minute or an expired contract. Fix: `RollStitcher.SeamCovered` names the dropped-but-stored minutes (snapshot sessions < 30 bars excluded), `SeriesRTHHoles` judges a minute missing only if NO contract in the stitch stores it. The stitched series itself is NOT changed (the gate does not move the mentor's numbers). Pins: `TestRollStitcherSeamCoveredNamesStoredMinutesTheCutDropped`, `TestRollSeamMinutesStoredByTheHeadAreNotAHoleAtTheProductionSeed` (real store, real `mentorSeedAtStart`), negative control `TestRollSeamMinutesStoredByNobodyStillBlockWithAnHonestRemedy`. Probe: for every "missing" verdict computed over a DERIVED series ask whether the minute is absent from the source or only from our derivation of it; for every remedy sentence ask whether the action named can reach the thing (replay depth, expired contract) and does the verdict re-measure after it (the seed measures only at start: an import needs a restart).
  - (D1b) Remedies are per hole: `IntegrityHole.Remedy` / `IntegrityActionFor` (reload only for a stretch NT8 can still replay; "no NT8 reload reaches this stretch" + import + the exact CT moment it clears by itself otherwise). `ClearsAtMs` is READ from the calendar (`windowClearsAtLocked`), pinned exact by `TestClearsAtIsTheExactMomentTheHoleLeavesTheWindow`. The tracker's key-level leg now stops at the same 90-day reach as the seeded-series leg (`TestKeyLevelLegStopsAtTheSameReachAsTheSeededSeriesLeg`; round 3 held it 100 days).
  - (D2) A window derived from the wrong reader. The "34 four-hour candles" deep window assumed the AI/planner/Picture/agent paths build their 4h from the 1m store; they read a NATIVE 4h frame, so it was too wide for the 4h and too narrow for the planner (`plannerCandleTapeBars` = 12000, `structureMapBarsAsk` = 2500). `IntegrityDeepOpenMin` = 12000 with a per-reader table in `bar_integrity.go`; pinned to the code by `TestIntegrityWindowsEqualTheCodeTheyDescribe`. Probe: write the reader/source/lookback table first, then the constant.
  - (D3) A banner broader than the pause. `/api/health trading_paused` now carries `scope` (widest) and `scopes`, only for symbols some RUNNING trader trades, and the banner names a narrower scope (`TestHealthTradingPausedCarriesTheScopeAndIgnoresUntradedSymbols`, `DataPausedBanner.test.tsx`). Probe: a status line must claim exactly what the gate refuses, for exactly the actors that exist.

For a MENTOR verdict an RTH hole inside the 1500-minute window was stamped with the window-exit instant, but at that instant the key-level leg picks the hole up and it pauses until the minutes are filled or it leaves the 90-day reach: the refusal text, the owner push and `/api/health clears_at` promised 10-28 11:30 and the pause ran to 01-25. `integrity()` now takes the LATER of the window exit and `ToMs + IntegritySeedReachDays` when `keyLevels` and the hole has RTH minutes. Probe: for every printed "resumes at T", re-run the verdict at T-1 min, T, and a few days after the earlier of two candidate Ts; the promise must hold at all of them.

Now `PausedView.Scopes` lists every blocked leg and `WidestPausedScope` names the widest (mentor + deep = `all_entries`: no path is left); the handler notes every leg of every view. Pins `TestScopeNamesEveryBlockedLegAndNeverUnderclaims`, `TestWidestPausedScopeRanksTheLegs`, `TestHealthScopeCarriesEveryBlockedLegAndNeverHidesTheMentorPause`. Probe: when a status picks ONE of several simultaneous causes, ask which cause a reader would be wrongly reassured about.

Probe: delete each guard; if nothing goes red, the comment describing it is a claim, not a fact.
  - Round-6 review fix, #55 (same class: owner-facing text that describes a pause the gate does not hold):

The log tail "Resumes by itself once the bars are measured filled" was also false for a retired hole, which ends at its printed clear time or on an import.
